subject: QBR capacity gap analysis & playbook
messages:
From: Nora Patel <procurement@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity and economics data for QBR & renewal

Hi Tessa / Laura,

As we prep for our renewal conversation next month, procurement needs a concise packet for our finance and SRE teams. Could you provide: a committed capacity proposal (GPU hours/month), 3-tier utilization scenarios (current / target / stress), unit economics (per-token and per-inference GPU $), and an estimate of realized savings from batching + prefix/KV caching under our typical request mix?

We also need historical 90-day tail latency percentiles (p95/p99) and any proposed SLA exceptions or credits if we move to a lower-cost committed plan. Please indicate what numbers are firm vs. modeled.

Can you send this by COB next Friday (Aug 6)? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min sync with the SRE and finance leads.

Thanks,
Nora Patel
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Analytics

Subject: Re: Capacity and economics data for QBR & renewal

Nora — thanks for the ask. For quick context: Nimbus currently consumes a mix of steady-state signed reserved slots plus periodic bursts on shared pools. From infra logs (past 90d): average GPU utilization on reserved pools: 64% (std dev 11%); observed p95 latency at 204 tokens: 420ms; p99: 1.2s.

We'll include those exact extracts in the packet. For committed sizing: we should present three options — Moderate (current baseline + 10%), Growth (baseline + 35%), and Aggressive (baseline + 80%) — with expected utilization after auto-scaling and target batching. Laura

— Laura Bennett
VP, Infrastructure Partnerships
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity and economics data for QBR & renewal

Attaching capacity_model_v3.xlsx and a short memo (gpu_unit_econ.md) with the modeling assumptions. High level numbers from the model (all USD):

- Current effective GPU cost per active hour (shared pool blended): $7.40/hr
- Committed (reserved) price we can offer at scale: $5.60/hr
- Token-level cost (text-gen baseline, 8k context, 16-bit): ~ $0.00092/token (hosted mix)
- Batching effects: expected token cost reduction 12-22% depending on tail percentiles and request size distribution; we modeled a conservative 14% for Moderate and 20% for Aggressive.
- Prefix/KV caching: for customers with repeat-session patterns (Nimbus has ~28% repeat prefix), effective per-token compute reduction ~9-12% on matching requests.
- Total modeled per-token saving if we combine batching + caching + reserved pricing: 28-40% (scenario dependent).
- Utilization targets post-commit: Moderate 72% (expected), Growth 78%, Aggressive 86%; above 85% we recommend idle buffer and burst capacity to maintain p99 latency SLAs.

Open items for the packet: explicit credit schedule for missed p99 SLA, detailed surge pricing during major events, and an annex on model quantization/precision options (we can propose a quantized variant for non-critical batch workloads that reduces cost further).

attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx, gpu_unit_econ.md
— Rishi
Sr Director, Applied ML & Inference Economics

Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity and economics data for QBR & renewal

Nora — sending the consolidated QBR playbook draft for procurement review (attached). Highlights below and a recommended ask for your finance team: 

- Recommended committed tiers (monthly GPU-hours, vGPU-eq): Moderate = 42k hrs (baseline+10%), Growth = 57k hrs (baseline+35%), Aggressive = 76k hrs (baseline+80%).
- Modeled blended unit economics (Moderate): $0.00066/token after reserved pricing and conservative batching (14%) and caching (9%). Growth/Aggressive show $0.00056 and $0.00042/token respectively.
- SLA proposal: p99 <= 1.1s for Moderate & Growth; for Aggressive we propose p99 <= 1.4s with guaranteed burst capacity to avoid tail events. SLA credits: sliding scale starting at 5% credit for single-month violations.
- Negotiation levers: multi-month commit (6/12 mo), flexible burst pool floor, and pilot quantized workloads (non-prod) to realize additional 6-12% savings.

Requesting a follow-up 30-min sync between your SRE and our infra/econ team next week to walk the numbers. Link to draft packet and supporting models below. If okay, we'll also prepare a one-page finance summary for internal sign-off.

Attachments: qbr_consolidated_playbook.docx
